messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected — service=\"inference-api/streaming\" window=11m p99=2800ms (baseline 450ms). Auto-created INC-4521. Paging on-call.

Priya (on-call): I’m on it. Seeing a bump in 504/streaming stalls in the dashboard, several customer sessions timed out. Kicking off triage.

Alex: on the control-plane side — seeing elevated latencies for config fetch and auth token validation. Request fanout to config service spiked ~x6.

Jen (SRE): Can someone share the slow query details for the tokenstore/db? I’ll start tailing proxy logs.

Riley (EngOps): quick check I ran: `SELECT count(*) FROM config_fetch_queue WHERE status='pending'` => 724000 (approx). Also seeing replication lag on replicas 2/3.

Alex: stack traces show time spent waiting on `config-service:fetch` and then a bunch of retries. Looks like feature-flag traffic is causing a frequent full-config fetch per request.

Priya (on-call): customer-impact? are we blocking all streaming or subset?

Nina (PM): Customers: 0.6% of active streaming sessions observed stalls/reconnects; top affected tenants are marketplace-prod and docs-search. SLA alerts from one customer.

Wei (DataEng): metrics: config fetch 95th went from 30ms -> 700ms, p99 -> 1800ms. DB CPU high, lots of `SELECT` on small table with large fanout.

Jen (SRE): hypothesis: new feature flag rollout (recent canary) caused per-request full config evaluation which fans out to DB. That + auth tokenstore lookups is thrashing DB leading to backpressure on inference control-plane, causing streaming stalls at p99.

Priya (on-call): immediate mitigations we can do now?

Alex: quick wins: 1) toggle feature-flag fallback to legacy eval (roll back canary), 2) enable short-circuit cache for config-service (serve stale 5s), 3) throttle outgoing config fetch by token for 30m.

Riley (EngOps): I can flip the cache setting and apply a per-service rate-limit. Patch I’ll run: 
```
# enable short-circuit cache
kubectl -n controlplane set env deploy/config-service CONFIG_CACHE_TTL=5
# apply token-level rate limit
curl -XPOST https://ops-api/rate-limits -d '{"service":"config-service","rule":"per-token:10/s"}'
```

Priya (on-call): Alex — can you rollback the feature flag? Which flag is it?

Alex: flag = `ff_new_routing_v2`. Rolling back via flags console now.

incident-bot: Action logged: Priya (on-call) initiated mitigation steps. Tags: "p99", "config-fetch", "feature-flag-rollback".

Riley (EngOps): cache TTL set, rate-limit pushed. Watching dashboards.

Jen (SRE): inspecting streaming worker logs — I see error pattern `upstream_timeout` correlated with `config-fetch` retries. Once cache TTL applied, error rate dropped from 1.8% -> 0.2% in 2m.

Nina (PM): notifying affected customers with status page note: "Investigating intermittent streaming stalls; mitigations in progress."

Priya (on-call): Sam — if this re-escalates handoff in 30m? I’ll stay on until stabilized for at least 20m.

Sam (backup-oncall): standing by. If p99 > 1.5s after mitigations we should consider routing traffic to dedicated lanes for high-SLO tenants.

Alex: also pushed a temporary auth-token cache on gateway to reduce tokenstore lookups: `AUTH_TOKEN_CACHE=120s` — small TTL but should reduce DB pressure.

Wei (DataEng): DB metrics after mitigations: CPU down 45%, replica lag gone, pending config_fetch_queue -> 6k (from 724k). Good signal.

incident-bot: Update INC-4521: mitigations applied (feature-flag rollback, cache TTL, rate-limits), p99 dropped to 480ms in 6m window.

Priya (on-call): Customer impact reduced to 0.03% streaming stalls. Marking incident as "mitigated" but not closed — need a follow-up postmortem and action items.

Jen (SRE): Root cause (preliminary): regression from a canaryed feature that triggered per-request full config evaluation + insufficient token caching -> DB/replica thrash -> control-plane backpressure -> streaming tail stalls.

Nina (PM): immediate follow-ups: 1) freeze rollout of `ff_new_routing_v2`, 2) widen canary testing to include load-sim, 3) notify sales for impacted customers.

Riley (EngOps): Ops follow-ups: add per-service backpressure (circuit-breaker) and telemetry on config fanout; ensure config-service serves stale config under load.

Alex: dev follow-ups: add local evaluation cache, reduce synchronous DB calls in hot path, add unit test for config fanout bound.

Priya (on-call): handoff notes for next on-call (Sam): mitigations applied, watch `inference-api.streaming.p99`, `config-service.fetch_queue`, and `tokenstore.latency`. If p99 creeps above 900ms -> page.

Sam (backup-oncall): acknowledged. I’ll monitor and start the postmortem doc when we close.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4521 status: MITIGATED (open for postmortem). Timeline: started=1749999999 mitigated=1749990102.

Priya (on-call): thanks team. Postmortem owners: Jen (SRE), Alex (Eng), Nina (PM). I'll add initial notes to the postmortem draft.

Wei (DataEng): logging query samples and slow statements to the postmortem. Attaching sample slow query: `SELECT * FROM tenant_config WHERE tenant_id = ?` executed 1.2M times in 10m window.

Nina (PM): customer comms drafted, will send once postmortem has timeline and impact numbers.

Jen (SRE): next steps assigned in Jira: CP-981 (circuit-breaker), CP-982 (config cache fallback), CP-983 (canary load tests).

Priya (on-call): closing active paging loop. If anything regresses ping `#incidents` and page oncall. Good work all. :thumbsup:
